theory.intro: Because $\sin\theta=\sin(180^{\circ}-\theta)$, two angles share the same sine. The calculator's $\sin^{-1}$ returns only the acute one, so the obtuse angle is $180^{\circ}-\theta$. Decide from the diagram or the wording which one the triangle needs.
facts: $\sin\theta=\sin(180^{\circ}-\theta)$, so an acute angle and its obtuse partner have exactly the same sine.
The calculator's $\sin^{-1}$ key always returns the acute angle, never the obtuse one.
Subtract the calculator's value from $180^{\circ}$ to get the obtuse solution.
The largest angle of a triangle lies opposite the longest side, so only that angle can be obtuse.
If the side opposite the unknown angle is shorter than the side opposite the known angle, the unknown angle must be acute.
A triangle cannot have two obtuse angles, so a given obtuse angle rules out a second one.
Keep the full calculator value in the working and round only on the last line.
steps: Write the sine rule with sin on top
Substitute the known angle and the two sides
Make sin of the unknown angle the subject
Take the inverse sine to get the acute angle
Decide whether the triangle needs the acute angle, the obtuse angle, or both
Subtract the acute angle from 180 degrees for the obtuse solution

foundation.solution_text:
$\theta$ is opposite the $10$ cm side and $25^{\circ}$ is opposite the $6$ cm side.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{10}=\dfrac{\sin 25^{\circ}}{6}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{10\sin 25^{\circ}}{6}$
$=0.70436\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $44.7781\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\theta$ is obtuse.
$\theta=180^{\circ}-44.7781\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 135^{\circ}$

$\theta$ is opposite the $14$ cm side and $32^{\circ}$ is opposite the $9$ cm side.

$=0.82431\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $55.5194\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\theta$ is obtuse.
$\theta=180^{\circ}-55.5194\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 124^{\circ}$

$\theta$ is opposite the $13$ m side and $30^{\circ}$ is opposite the $9$ m side.

$=0.72222\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $46.2383\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\theta$ is obtuse.
$\theta=180^{\circ}-46.2383\ldots^{\circ}$

The inverse sine gives the acute angle $43.4963\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\theta$ is obtuse.

The angle opposite the $11$ cm side is $\angle AQC$ in one triangle and $\angle APC$ in the other.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{11}=\dfrac{\sin 30^{\circ}}{7}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{11\sin 30^{\circ}}{7}$
$=0.78571\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $51.7867\ldots^{\circ}$, which is $\angle AQC$.
$\angle AQC\approx 52^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner has the same sine, and it is $\angle APC$.
$\angle APC=180^{\circ}-51.7867\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 128^{\circ}$

The angle opposite the $13$ m side is $\angle AQC$ in one triangle and $\angle APC$ in the other.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{13}=\dfrac{\sin 44^{\circ}}{10}$

$=0.90305\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $64.5627\ldots^{\circ}$, which is $\angle AQC$.
$\angle AQC\approx 65^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner has the same sine, and it is $\angle APC$.
$\angle APC=180^{\circ}-64.5627\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 115^{\circ}$

development.solution_text:
$\angle ABC$ is opposite the $17$ cm side and $35^{\circ}$ is opposite the $12$ cm side.
$\dfrac{\sin\angle ABC}{17}=\dfrac{\sin 35^{\circ}}{12}$
$\sin\angle ABC=\dfrac{17\sin 35^{\circ}}{12}$
$=0.81256\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $54.3474\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\angle ABC$ is obtuse.
$\angle ABC=180^{\circ}-54.3474\ldots^{\circ}$
$=125.6525\ldots^{\circ}$
The three angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\angle ACB=180^{\circ}-35^{\circ}-125.6525\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 19^{\circ}$

$\angle ABC$ is opposite the $15$ m side and $41^{\circ}$ is opposite the $11$ m side.
$\dfrac{\sin\angle ABC}{15}=\dfrac{\sin 41^{\circ}}{11}$
$\sin\angle ABC=\dfrac{15\sin 41^{\circ}}{11}$
$=0.89462\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $63.4604\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\angle ABC$ is obtuse.
$\angle ABC=180^{\circ}-63.4604\ldots^{\circ}$
$=116.5395\ldots^{\circ}$
The three angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\angle ACB=180^{\circ}-41^{\circ}-116.5395\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 22^{\circ}$

$\angle PQR$ is opposite the $19$ cm side and $108^{\circ}$ is opposite the $26$ cm side.
$\dfrac{\sin\angle PQR}{19}=\dfrac{\sin 108^{\circ}}{26}$
$\sin\angle PQR=\dfrac{19\sin 108^{\circ}}{26}$
$=0.69500\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $44.0273\ldots^{\circ}$.
$\angle PQR\approx 44^{\circ}$
The obtuse solution $135.9726\ldots^{\circ}$ is rejected because $\angle QPR$ is already obtuse, and a triangle cannot contain two obtuse angles.

$\angle XYZ$ is opposite the $14$ m side and $40^{\circ}$ is opposite the $21$ m side.
$\dfrac{\sin\angle XYZ}{14}=\dfrac{\sin 40^{\circ}}{21}$
$\sin\angle XYZ=\dfrac{14\sin 40^{\circ}}{21}$
$=0.42852\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $25.3739\ldots^{\circ}$.
$\angle XYZ\approx 25^{\circ}$
The obtuse solution $154.6260\ldots^{\circ}$ is rejected because $XZ=14$ m is shorter than $YZ=21$ m, so $\angle XYZ$ must be smaller than the $40^{\circ}$ opposite $YZ$.

The angle at $B$ is opposite the $9$ km side and $29^{\circ}$ is opposite the $6.5$ km side.

$\sin B=\dfrac{9\sin 29^{\circ}}{6.5}$
$=0.67127\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $42.1655\ldots^{\circ}$, and the angle at $B$ is obtuse.
$B=180^{\circ}-42.1655\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 138^{\circ}$

$=0.83969\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $57.1076\ldots^{\circ}$, which is $\angle AQC$.
$\angle AQC\approx 57^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner has the same sine, and it is $\angle APC$.

$\approx 123^{\circ}$

$\theta$ is opposite the $26$ cm side and $33^{\circ}$ is opposite the $19$ cm side.

$\sin\theta=\dfrac{26\sin 33^{\circ}}{19}$

The inverse sine gives the acute angle $48.1844\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\theta$ is obtuse.
$\theta=180^{\circ}-48.1844\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 132^{\circ}$

mastery.solution_text:
The angle at $B$ is opposite the $31$ m side and $37^{\circ}$ is opposite the $23$ m side.
$\dfrac{\sin B}{31}=\dfrac{\sin 37^{\circ}}{23}$
$\sin B=\dfrac{31\sin 37^{\circ}}{23}$
$=0.81114\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $54.2076\ldots^{\circ}$, and the corner at $B$ is obtuse.
$B=180^{\circ}-54.2076\ldots^{\circ}$
$=125.7923\ldots^{\circ}$
The three corners add to $180^{\circ}$.
$C=180^{\circ}-37^{\circ}-125.7923\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 17^{\circ}$

$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{18}=\dfrac{\sin 42^{\circ}}{13}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{18\sin 42^{\circ}}{13}$
$=0.92648\ldots$
The inverse sine gives $\angle AQC=67.8938\ldots^{\circ}$, and its obtuse partner is $\angle APC=112.1061\ldots^{\circ}$.
In triangle $AQC$ the angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\angle ACQ=180^{\circ}-42^{\circ}-67.8938\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 70^{\circ}$
In triangle $APC$ the angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\angle ACP=180^{\circ}-42^{\circ}-112.1061\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 26^{\circ}$

$\angle PQR$ is opposite the $34$ m side and $95^{\circ}$ is opposite the $45$ m side.
$\dfrac{\sin\angle PQR}{34}=\dfrac{\sin 95^{\circ}}{45}$
$\sin\angle PQR=\dfrac{34\sin 95^{\circ}}{45}$
$=0.75268\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $48.8231\ldots^{\circ}$.
$\angle PQR\approx 49^{\circ}$
The surveyor is wrong: $\angle QPR=95^{\circ}$ is already obtuse, so the obtuse solution $131.1768\ldots^{\circ}$ would make the angle sum exceed $180^{\circ}$.
